title: Wajdi and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Wajdi tries to give light to Jala and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Jala, who was clearness after rain, lived in fear of the dark, and Wajdi, who carried the ecstasy of finding, standing beyond the self, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Wajdi's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Wajdi pressed the dead lamp into Jala's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Wajdi stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Wajdi learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
